skill.name: meeting-insights-analyzer
skill.description: Analyzes meeting transcripts to identify communication patterns, speaking habits, facilitation style, and coaching opportunities. It helps users review conflict avoidance, filler words, interruptions, listening behavior, and progress over time.
skill.summary: Review meeting transcripts for communication patterns, examples, and practical coaching feedback.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

content.value_statement: Meeting transcripts are hard to review consistently across many calls. This skill turns transcripts into focused communication feedback with examples and next steps.
actual_capabilities: Scans transcript files in common text, subtitle, markdown, and document formats when available.
Identifies conflict avoidance, hedging, interruptions, filler words, and active listening cues.
Calculates speaking ratios, turn length, question rates, and interruption counts from labeled transcripts.
Compares meetings over time to show changes in communication behavior.
Produces timestamped examples, impact explanations, and suggested alternative phrasing.
limitations: Needs accurate speaker labels and timestamps for reliable per-person metrics.
Does not create transcripts from raw audio or video by itself.
Cannot verify intent behind a statement without meeting context.
Results depend on the quality and completeness of the provided files.

use_cases.title: Improve Team Facilitation
use_cases.description: Review recurring team meetings to see who speaks, how decisions are handled, and where quieter participants need support.

use_cases.title: Prepare Coaching Feedback
use_cases.description: Find specific examples of communication strengths, missed listening moments, and practical improvement areas for a client.

use_cases.title: Track Personal Communication Growth
use_cases.description: Compare meeting transcripts across months or quarters to measure progress on interruptions, questions, and direct feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Recent Meetings
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a folder of transcripts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the meeting transcripts in this folder. Summarize my main communication patterns and include specific examples.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused analysis of a known habit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Look for moments where I interrupted others or used filler words. Count the pattern and show the strongest examples.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Time Periods
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my Q1 and Q2 meeting transcripts. Show whether my listening skills improved and where gaps remain.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Development Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced coaching plan from repeated patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these transcripts for facilitation, conflict avoidance, speaking ratio, and listening. Create a prioritized communication development plan.

output_examples.input: Analyze my last month of team meetings for facilitation style.
output_examples.output: A summary of meeting count, speaking ratio, question patterns, inclusion of quieter participants, key strengths, and three focused improvement actions.

output_examples.input: Tell me where I avoided conflict in these one-on-one meetings.
output_examples.output: A conflict-avoidance report with frequency, timestamped transcript examples, impact notes, and clearer alternative phrasing.

output_examples.input: Compare my meetings from Q1 and Q2 for listening progress.
output_examples.output: A trend comparison showing interruption changes, clarifying question frequency, active listening examples, and remaining growth areas.

best_practices: Use transcripts with consistent filenames, dates, speaker labels, and timestamps.
Ask about one or two behaviors at a time when you need deeper feedback.
Review sensitive meeting data locally and remove transcripts that should not be analyzed.
anti_patterns: Do not use incomplete transcripts to make performance claims about a person.
Do not treat the analysis as proof of intent without broader meeting context.
Do not combine unrelated meeting types when comparing communication trends.

faq.question: What transcript formats can this skill review?
faq.answer: It is designed for common transcript files such as text, markdown, subtitles, and document exports.

faq.question: Can it analyze raw meeting recordings?
faq.answer: No. It needs transcripts or readable meeting notes, not raw audio or video files.

faq.question: Does it identify who spoke in each meeting?
faq.answer: It can do this when transcripts include clear speaker labels. Unlabeled transcripts reduce accuracy.

faq.question: Can it compare progress over time?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide transcripts grouped by period so it can compare patterns across meetings.

faq.question: Is this a performance review generator?
faq.answer: It can provide examples for reflection, but human judgment should guide formal performance feedback.

faq.question: How should sensitive transcripts be handled?
faq.answer: Keep sensitive meeting files local, limit access, and remove data that should not be reviewed.
